title: ClawDOS – An AI coding agent for DOS
lede: ClawDOS is a Claude coding agent that runs natively on an IBM PC XT, with an 8088 CPU and 640K of RAM, handing only TLS to a bridge machine.

points: HARNESS.EXE, a 176 KB DOS program, builds Messages API requests, parses the streamed reply, runs 18 tools and stores chats on disk.
The agent edits files and compiles with Turbo C, stepping out of memory so the compiler has the machine to itself.
A timer interrupt captures CGA video memory, which the 8088 encodes as a PNG so Claude can see program output.
Memories and skills are plain text files; a safe mode asks before any file, memory or port change.
The author says Claude wrote the whole repo; it is GPLv3 and runs in 86Box or on real hardware.

points.text: One commenter wants agents for legacy Windows XP and 7 machines, since most current agents need Windows 10 1809 or newer.
Many enjoy dropping agents into odd environments; one built a Win32 agent and watched a model realise it was on NT 4.0.
Another suggests demoscene-style projects would work better driven remotely, since the harness competes with them for resources.
